purpose: Prove, on the target host, that the gemma3 row decodes on the CPU on Windows even with a working CUDA device, and record the lane + cadence the CUDA lane will be compared against.

host.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (compute capability 8.6)

observed.plan_reason: windowed-attention row (gemma3): the only validated dense lane is Metal-resident; no CPU dense plan exists for this arch — serve chats via the runnable bridge on this host; failing closed to safe path

cadence_probe.prompt: Name the capital of France in one word.
cadence_probe.note: Wall time covers prefill of 18 tokens plus 2 generated tokens on the runnable CPU bridge. Recorded as an OBSERVATION of the baseline lane on this host, not as a benchmark: no thread pinning, no repeat runs, no isolation discipline. It is here to size the gap, not to be quoted.

conclusion: The premise holds. CUDA is present, selected, and the resident engine is even warmed — the gemma3 row is refused by routing, not by the absence of a device. Both the plan disclosure and the served response independently name the runnable CPU lane.
not_claimed: No throughput claim for either lane.
No parity claim — this phase captures a lane identity and a cadence observation only.
No statement about any gemma3 row or quant other than 1B Q8_0.
